newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast spot gasoline edges up with APIs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast spot gasoline edges up with APIs.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast gasoline edged higher amid concerns of modestly lower supplies, traders said.
The market was traded lightly Tuesday, ahead of a late afternoon report from the American Petroleum Institute (API).
But when the report was issued, the market firmed in the wake of a 1.6 million- barrel-drop in West Coast gasoline supplies.
Some traders took advantage of the tightening inventories to lift gasoline offers a slight 1.00 cent a gallon late Tuesday.
"The gasoline was up with the (API) numbers," one broker said.
Bids for Los Angeles CARB gasoline rose 1.50 cent a gallon to 57.50 cents, traders said, with offers up one cent.
Buyers of conventional grade gasoline, for sale in Reno, Nevada, offered to pay 54.50 cents a gallon, a 1.50 cent rise from Monday levels, traders said.
